newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DORTMUND WARY OF AUXERRE DESPITE FIRST LEG WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND WARY OF AUXERRE DESPITE FIRST LEG WIN.

text.p: Despite a comfortable 3-1 win in the first leg, German champions Dortmund are not taking anything for granted before their European Cup quarter-final second leg match in Auxerre on Wednesday.
Borussia lost 4-1 to VfB Stuttgart in the Bundesliga on Saturday. A similar defeat in France would see Auxerre advance to the last four.
"It's very simple, we must avoid that kind of result," said Dortmund captain Matthias Sammer who missed the first leg with a calf injury.
"We must not go into the match thinking we have already done the hardest part," he said. "We will have to fight for 90 minutes because that's what Auxerre will do. They have nothing to lose."
Dortmund will be without defender Stefan Reuter, suspended after being sent off in the first leg for a second bookable offence.

Portuguese midfielder Paulo Sousa and striker Karlheinz Riedle, who both missed Saturday's match with injuries, should play but Brazilian defender Julio Cesar, still recovering from a knee operation at Christmas, will not return.
Auxerre, who warmed up by beating Cannes 3-1 on Friday, are hoping goalkeeper Lionel Charbonnier will be able to play despite a painful right shoulder.
Charbonnier, defender Franck Silvestre and midfielder Moussa Saib all missed the match against Cannes but trainer Guy Roux said they should start.

The French club, playing in the European Cup for the first time, will remember their UEFA Cup semifinal with Dortmund in 1993 in which they fought back from a two-goal first-leg deficit only to lose on penalties.

"It will be tough but it's not impossible," said captain Silvestre. "We'll have to be at 200 per cent from the start but at the same time we'll have to be patient and careful. We know we need goals but if we let them score it will be all over."

France have had a team in the European Cup semifinals in each of the last four years and Auxerre, who impressed in this year's campaign by beating Ajax Amsterdam, dream of following the example of Marseille, Paris St Germain, Monaco and Nantes.
"We all want to go for it, to achieve something exceptional, and we believe we can make it," striker Bernard Diomede said. "Otherwise, there would be no point in starting the match."
But Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld sounded reasonably confident despite his side's defeat at the weekend.
"This is our chance to join Europe's footballing elite," he said. "We have to take out our frustration at losing to Stuttgart on Auxerre."

Auxerre (probable) - Lionel Charbonnier, Alain Goma, Franck Silvestre (captain), Frederic Danjou, Taribo West, Philippe Violeau, Sabri Lamouchi, Moussa Saib, Antoine Sibierski, Lilian Laslandes, Bernard Diomede.

Dortmund (probable) - Stefan Klos, Joerg Heinrich, Juergen Kohler, Matthias Sammer (captain), Martin Kree, Lars Ricken, Paul Lambert, Paulo Sousa, Andreas Moeller, Karlheinz Riedle, Stephane Chapuisat.
